::: {.why}
Reporting a speedup without decomposing it is how people conclude that C++ is fast when what they measured was that dictionaries are slow, and separating the two is worth an hour.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Decompose the Python-to-C++ speedup into interpreter overhead and data structure difference.
- Say what you would do to close most of the gap without leaving Python, and measure it.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Isolate the causes: write a third version in Python using the same data structures as your C++ book, and a fourth using numba on the hot loop. Time all four on the same replay. The four numbers separate the language from the layout, which is the honest decomposition.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Draw the conclusion for your own work: with your latencies from day 304, decide whether any part of your production stack needs C++ at all. The answer is almost certainly no, and being able to say that with measurements behind it is a better interview answer than claiming to be a C++ programmer.
:::
:::
